scope: MEAS: independent numerical, report/source, published note/bar-map, actual-sheet and visual review; not aural review.

report.finding: Report agrees with final 3921-event / 12-source-voice checks, 68-bar once-through order and five-page pack. Source edition, D-trumpet octave repair, preserved chorus/organ identities and the rejected compressed final-quarter false positive are accurately distinguished. The fitted q268 constraint is not described as independent validation.

barMap.finding: All 3921 note bar/voice indices resolve, durations are positive and bar times strictly increase. Actual SVG/index sets are exactly 1–68. Pages 1 and 5 were inspected: F-basset-horn and D-trumpet written transpositions are labelled, SATB/lyrics remain, the chorus stops after bar 65 and orchestral material continues through 68. The final separate lower-string quarter and following rests are retained. Listen cues use seconds, not structured bar pointers.

overlays.finding: No gross pitch/order mismatch identified in current timing windows. The upper final tutti near 108.5 s is followed by a distinct D3/D4 lower-string renewal near 108.917 s; q268–269 is no longer compressed into the earlier approximately 0.081 s interval. Its written-quarter duration to 109.358 s is not a measured bow release.

source.edition: Breitkopf & Härtel, 1877, edited by Johannes Brahms; Süssmayr completion
source.encoder: Martin Norbäck; 2014 update by Francisco Vila

registerInterpretation.finding: The D-trumpet standard is a major second above written pitch. Given the source’s written C5/C4 and old MIDI D4/D3, the specific +12 correction restores D5/D4. This is not a blanket octave rule for all historical brass. F-basset-horn and choral registers remain as encoded.

version.finding: Complete Dies irae in the identified Süssmayr-version source, 68 bars once, without a fabricated repeat/cut. The single original organ/orchestral-bass staff remains one source line; no inferred cello, double-bass, trombone doubling or realised continuo is invented. No gross arrangement mismatch identified.
version.physicalPerformingEdition: Unknown; neither a Mozart-autograph-only source nor Walter’s marked conducting edition is claimed.

limitations: MEAS: No aural review, build or browser integration check performed by VerS. Source-backed transposition does not independently isolate the recorded trumpet line; fitting constraints and warped durations are not independent performance certification.
